questions.prompt: Sacrosanctum Concilium's ressourcement (return-to-the-sources) principle draws on the Church's most ancient liturgical witnesses. St. Justin Martyr's First Apology (ch. 65-67), written around 155 AD, describes which elements of the Sunday assembly that the Council's reform sought to recover?
choices: Readings from the 'memoirs of the apostles,' a common prayer, and the president giving thanks over bread and wine mixed with water
A private Mass celebrated silently with no congregation present
A liturgy conducted entirely in a language unknown to the congregation
An annual, not weekly, celebration of the Eucharist
questions.correctAnswer: Readings from the 'memoirs of the apostles,' a common prayer, and the president giving thanks over bread and wine mixed with water
questions.explanation: Justin Martyr's description -- readings, a homily, common prayers, and the president's thanksgiving over the gifts -- is one of the earliest detailed accounts of the Christian Sunday assembly, and the Council's ressourcement principle explicitly looked to sources like this to recover the liturgy's ancient shape.
questions.hint: Justin describes readings, a homily, common prayers, and the president giving thanks over the gifts -- one of the earliest snapshots of what Sunday Mass actually looked like.
